lines.trans: Do you remember Senior Ye-jin's story from that night—the one you edited out?
An accident happens whenever three bad coincidences line up in a row.
Of all nights, Ye-jin was worked up and drinking on an empty stomach.
I should have told everyone to go straight home, except I was craving a drink too.
Whenever I liked someone, I used to spill everything to you, Joon-mo.
Since Senior Ye-jin says she likes Senior Joon-mo, I refuse to let just the two of you leave!
Why do you keep weaving back and forth in zigzags—please walk straight!
Walk straight yourself—go back to your own house already!
My heart feels way too uneasy, so I will watch the two of you get inside safely before going home.
I figured if I alone forgot, it could be as if nothing happened—except this guy remembered.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 만약에 기억을 하는데도 아무 반응을 안 보이고 있는 거라면, 준모가 그 진심을 편집해버렸단 얘기 아닐까?
examples.trans: If he remembers everything and still shows no reaction, does that not mean Joon-mo edited out those feelings?
This expression comes from 'edited right out'.

meanings.note: refers to a previously mentioned or specific day

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
I don't have time that day.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'nights' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 선배님이 편집해버린 그날 밤 예진 선배님 이야기 기억나세요?
examples.trans: Do you remember Senior Ye-jin's confession from that night—the one you edited out?
Here the word for 'story, confession' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나? 나 뮤직뱅크 탁예진 피디 기억나지?
examples.trans: Me? You remember Music Bank producer Tak Ye-jin, right?
This expression comes from 'you remember, right?'.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 사고라는 건 하필이 세 번이면 일어난다.
examples.trans: An accident happens whenever three bad coincidences line up in a row.
Here the word for 'unlucky timing' is key.

examples.text: 수습 기간 중에 세 번 사고 치면 잘릴 수도 있대요.
examples.trans: I heard that if you cause trouble three times during probation, you can get fired.
The topic of three came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.
I want to stand up right now.
How about trying to stand up together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Native Korean numeral used with hours (시), age (살), and general counters.

examples.trans: It is ten o'clock now.
Please give me ten apples.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그날 예진이는 하필 열이 받았고 하필 빈속이었다.
examples.trans: Of all nights, Ye-jin was worked up and drinking on an empty stomach.
Here the word for 'had an empty stomach' is key.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그냥 집으로 가자고 했어야 했는데 나도 술이 땡겼다.
examples.trans: I should have told everyone to go straight home, except I was craving a drink too.
This expression comes from 'was craving'.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?
I like listening to music.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 내가 진짜 힘든 건, 내가 누구 좋아하면 너한테 다 털어놨었잖아.
examples.trans: What is truly hard for me is that whenever I liked someone, I used to spill everything to you.
This expression comes from 'used to confide, remember'.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: native Korean numeral; 둘이 means 'the two of them'

examples.trans: The two of us work together.
Two coffees, please.
I want to did you send? right now.
How about trying to did you send? together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.

examples.trans: I really dislike rainy days.
You hate waking up early in the morning, right?

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

examples.text: 자꾸 어디 넘어지고 또 칠칠맞게 뭐 하다 다쳤냐?
examples.trans: Always tripping somewhere—what clumsy thing were you doing to get hurt again?

examples.text: 걱정은 하지, 늘. 근데 왜 백승찬을 집에 자꾸 들이냐?
examples.trans: I always worry. Still, why do you keep letting Baek Seung-chan into the house?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Yes, he was weaving back and forth in zigzags.
Here the word for 'in a zigzag pattern' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 왜 자꾸 왔다 갔다 갈지자로 가시는지, 똑바로 가십시오!
examples.trans: Why do you keep weaving back and forth in zigzags—please walk straight!
Here the word for 'straight' is key.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Did you hear about this to my liking?
I was busy today because of to my liking.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 제가 마음이 영 불안해서 두 분 무사히 들어가시는 거 보고 들어가겠습니다.
examples.trans: My heart feels way too uneasy, so I will watch the two of you get inside safely before going home.
Here the word for 'really, altogether' is key.
I'm always anxious before an exam.
I feel a bit uneasy when I'm alone.

meanings.note: Attributive form of 둘 used directly before counter nouns (두 개, 두 사람).

examples.trans: Please give me two apples.
Let's meet at two o'clock.

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 제가 마음이 영 불안해서 두 분 무사히 들어가시는 거 보고 들어가겠습니다.
examples.trans: My heart feels way too uneasy, so I will watch the two of you get inside safely before going home.
Here the word for 'safely' is key.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나만 잊어버리면 없었던 일이 될 수 있다고 생각했는데, 하필 이 녀석이 기억하고 있었다.
examples.trans: I figured if I alone forgot, it could be as if nothing happened—except this guy remembered.
This expression comes from 'if I forget'.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아들이란 녀석이 조그만 스캔들에라도 휘말리면 이거 치명적인데!
examples.trans: if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!
Here the word for 'chap, fellow' is key.
Let's you remember, right? together today.
I worked hard to you remember, right? yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
